critical.issue: Field-name mismatch: OnboardingReq Pydantic model (server.py:924–930) accepts weekly_rides/confident_60min/self_rating but the review's Advanced payload sends weekly_hours/can_ride_60min/structured_before. Extra fields are silently dropped by Pydantic → an Advanced rider scores only 6 (from experience_years + longest_ride_min alone) → misclassified as Intermediate → recommended {id:'ride-stronger'} instead of the required {id:'ride-beyond',authored:true}. Fix: rename model fields OR accept both aliases (Field(alias=...) or model_config populate_by_name) so both wire-formats classify identically, and re-weight so structured_before+can_ride_60min contribute.

Ride-beyond entry (and all plan entries) is missing the `level` field. Review requires 'level Advanced' exposed here so onboarding can filter/recommend by level. Neither list_plans() output nor the ride-beyond doc surfaces {level:'Advanced'} even though _seed_authored on startup writes {'$set':{'level':'Advanced'}} for ride-beyond (server.py:2782). rca_of_issue: Bug 1 (Advanced onboarding recommends ride-stronger not ride-beyond): OnboardingReq Pydantic model in /app/backend/server.py lines 924–930 declares fields experience_years/weekly_rides/longest_ride_min/confident_60min/self_rating/goal. The review's Advanced payload sends weekly_hours=12, can_ride_60min=true, structured_before=true. Pydantic (v2 default) silently drops unknown keys, so the classifier sees experience_years=12 (→3) + weekly_rides=0 (→0) + longest_ride_min=240 (→3) + confident_60min=False (→0) + self_rating='new' (→0) = 6 → Intermediate. Mitigation: rename model fields to match the UI (weekly_hours, can_ride_60min, structured_before) OR use pydantic Field aliases + model_config(populate_by_name=True), and rebalance _classify_level to award +1.5 for structured_before and +1.5 for can_ride_60min so an Advanced profile crosses the 8-point threshold. Bug 2 (/api/plans no `level`): plans_admin.list_plans() likely projects only id/title/description/type/duration_weeks/week_count/updated_at — need to include `level` so the frontend can filter by rider level. server.py already writes {'level':'Advanced'} to the ride-beyond DB doc at startup (line 2782) — the field exists in Mongo but is not returned.
